_doc: Labeled corpus of melodic-variation transforms. A phrase A' is derived from phrase A by one or more named ops. Note format = [scale_degree, octave, duration_in_beats]. Phrases segmented by inter-onset gap (user's melody model). FOCUS on songs WITH LYRICS: carry the lyric line aligned 1-token-per-note (per the melisma format in melisma_examples.json / melisma_align.py) so rhyme-beats and which-syllable-gets-the-melisma line up with the notes. CANONICAL HOME is now Supabase parcels.melodies (columns phrases/palette/cadence/transforms added 2026-06-30, keyed by slug+section). This JSON is the STAGING/scratch format + definitions; named examples get migrated to the table. The 112 example stays here only (no slug).

rules.trim: drop final note(s) off the phrase tail on the repeat
rules.clip: drop leading note(s) / pickup off the phrase head (front version of trim)
rules.tag: add a note onto the end
rules.merge: fuse two adjacent same-pitch notes into one held note, same total duration (inverse of fill)
rules.fill: add internal note(s), subdividing the rhythm, same contour
rules.lift: raise only the final note (open ending)
rules.drop: lower only the final note (closed ending)
rules.step: transpose the whole phrase up/down a step (sequence)
rules.cross-graft: rhythm donor phrase + pitch donor phrase; when counts mismatch, repeat a pitch

axes._doc: Ops are the HOW (pitch/length transforms). These axes are the WHERE — metric + harmonic position — independently variable.
axes.rhythm: onset beats + durations of each note; the rhythmic profile of the phrase
axes.breaks: rests/gaps between phrases (isRest notes + inter-onset gaps) = the phrase boundaries
axes.rhyme-beats: which metric positions recur across phrases (e.g. both phrases start on the & of 2)
axes.chord-alignment: which notes land on a chord change and whether they sing the new chord's tone

phrase_architecture.112: musical sentence: idea (1) + repeat-of-idea (1) + continuation twice as long (2). The 1->1 leg is where variation ops usually live.

cadence._def: The cadence of a phrase = its FINAL NOTE (single note). Locked 2026-06-30.
cadence.open_closed: melodic classification by scale degree of the final note: closed = stable (1, sometimes 3); open = unstable (2,4,5,6,7 or any note below tonic like the low 6).
cadence.vs_chord: ALSO track the final note's role against the chord sounding under it: root/3rd/5th = chord tone (harmonically closed); anything else = non-chord tone (harmonically open). Melodic and harmonic verdicts often disagree — record both.
cadence.cadence_tag: SEPARATE concept: a recurring rhythmic ending figure (e.g. 0.5,1.25) shared across phrases, independent of pitch. Rhythm-axis, not a cadence pitch.

palette._def: Pitch inventory = which scale degrees the melody uses. Most melodies run on a tiny CORE (2-3 notes); this is a strong fingerprint and a mixing constraint (shared core -> clean graft).
palette.core: the 2-4 degrees carrying most of the melody, weighted by TIME on each degree (>= ~15% of note-duration)
palette.reach: occasional degrees it steps out to (low dip / high peak)
palette._octave_note: normalize octave per song (subtract the song's modal octave) before comparing stretch across songs; raw Hookpad octave anchors differ (some songs main-octave = 1, some = 0).

meta_patterns.front-anchored: answer keeps the OPENING constant and varies the final note (open vs closed). Classic question/answer; yearning. e.g. Wouldn't It Be Nice (front 4 notes identical, final 1->↓6).
meta_patterns.cadence-anchored: answer keeps the FINAL NOTE constant and varies the front. Judge by the final note (pitch), NOT the ending rhythm.
meta_patterns._axis: anchor = which end is held constant between a phrase and its answer, judged by the FINAL NOTE. Likely predicts feel; label on every example.
meta_patterns._quietriot_correction: Quiet Riot is NOT cadence-anchored: A ends ↓6, A' ends 1 (trim removed the ↓6) — final pitch CHANGES. What's constant there is the cadence-tag RHYTHM (0.5,1.25), a rhythm-axis pattern, not a pitch anchor.

examples.song: Quiet Riot - Come On Feel The Noise
examples.cadence_vs_chord: A ↓6 over vi = root (harmonically closed) though melodically open; A' 1 over V = non-chord tone (harmonically open) though melodically closed; B/B' 2 over I = non-chord tone (open both ways).
examples.notes: Both answers collapse 6 notes -> 4. Held constant is the cadence-TAG rhythm (0.5,1.25) on A' and B/B', NOT the final pitch (A ↓6 -> A' 1). So this is a cadence-tag/rhythm anchor, not a cadence-pitch anchor.

examples.song: The Beach Boys - Wouldn't It Be Nice
examples.lyric: wouldn't it be nice if we were older / then we wouldn't have to wait so long
examples.cadence_vs_chord: no chord data in this paste; melodic only. Final 1 (closed) -> ↓6 (open) is the yearning.
examples.notes: FRONT-anchored: front 4 notes held identical, final note varies 1->↓6 (closed->open). Answer-half internal pitches also shift 1->2 (mild step). TODO confirm trim count: my segmentation shows net -1 note in the answer half vs user's 'last two'.

examples.anchor: cadence (both phrases share the 5 7 1 7 body + eighth-run rhythm; front + tail vary)

final_notes.P1: 7 over I (open melodically, non-chord tone harmonically)
final_notes.P2: 6 over vi (open melodically, but ROOT of vi = harmonically closed)

examples.cadence_vs_chord: The headline disagreement: P2 ends on scale-degree 6 (open on paper) yet it's the root of the vi chord under it = a real harmonic arrival. Tracking both is what catches this.
examples.chord_alignment: P1 sits entirely under I. P2's tag note 6 lands ON the I->vi change (b9.5) and sings the vi root. Tag is harmonically placed, not decorative.
examples.notes: Confirms lift/drop is position-noted, not cadence-only (here lift is on the FIRST note). Steady eighth-note runner rhythm; both phrases enter on an off-beat pickup (rhyme-beat).
